title: Tools
text:
Free tools treat the soil horizon by horizon. Our advanced methods treat it as one connected system, continuous with depth and across the landscape, because that is how water, carbon and energy actually move.
  Everything runs in your browser. Uploaded data never leaves your device.

  Profile harmoniser
  Fit a physics-informed spline (phySpline) to irregular horizon data and harmonise it to standard depth intervals. Works for continuous properties (carbon, pH, clay) and for ordered classes such as texture.

  
    1. Your data
    
    
      Upload CSV
      Example: soil carbon

    Columns: profile id, top depth (cm), bottom depth (cm), then one or more property columns. Comma, semicolon or tab separated. Up to 20,000 rows.

      Intervals that extend past the bottom of a profile are averaged over the soil that is present and shown in amber. Blank means no soil in that interval.
      
    
  

  
    Need more than horizon-based harmonisation?
    Our advanced profile method treats the soil as one continuous system: much faster on large datasets, with uncertainty at every depth and boundary-aware profiles linked to water and heat flux.
    Get in touch →
  
  Method: Flynn, T., Rasaei, Z., Kostecki, R. (2026). Science of the Total Environment. doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2026.181621. Open R implementation: rafikisol package.




  Soil carbon stocks
  Calculate organic carbon stocks for many profiles at once, by summing horizons to fixed depths, with an optional equivalent soil mass basis for comparing sites or sampling dates.
  
    1. Your data
    
    
      Upload CSV
      Load example
    
    Columns: id, top (cm), bottom (cm), soc (%), bd (bulk density, g/cm³), and optionally cf (coarse fragments, % by volume).
  
  
    2. Settings
    
      Report to depths (cm)
      Reference soil mass (Mg/ha, optional)
    
    Equivalent soil mass: stock in the soil needed to reach the reference mass, regardless of depth. Useful when bulk density differs between sites or dates.
    Calculate
    
  
  
    
      Stocks (Mg C/ha)
      Download CSV
    
    
    
    Amber values: the profile is shallower than the reporting depth, so the stock covers only the soil that was sampled.
  
  
    Horizon sums can overestimate stocks
    Summing horizons assumes each layer is uniform. Our published work shows this can substantially overestimate carbon stocks compared with assessing the profile at every point. For baselines, credits or reporting, we calculate stocks from depth-continuous profiles with uncertainty.
    
    Get in touch →

  Sampling density
  Estimate how many samples you need to measure a field or site mean within a chosen margin of error, assuming simple random sampling.

        Coefficient of variation (%)

    Spatial variation changes the answer
    Random sampling ignores the fact that nearby soils are alike. We design optimised and stratified sampling schemes and management zones that reach the same precision with fewer samples.

  Pedodiversity
  Measure the taxonomic diversity of soils in an area: how many soil classes there are, and how evenly the area is shared between them. Compare several sites at once.
  
    Your soil classes
    
    
      Upload CSV
      Load example
      Calculate
    
    A column named class is required (any classification: soil orders, reference soil groups, series, map units). Add area or count to weight each row; without one, every row counts once (for example, one row per profile). Add site to compare several areas.
    
  
  
    
      
        Indices by site
        Download CSV
      
      
    
    
      
        
          Indices
          
        
        
      
      
        Share of each class
        
      
    
    
      Reading the indices
      Richness counts classes. Shannon (H′) rises with both more classes and more even shares. Evenness (J′) is Shannon relative to its maximum for that many classes, from 0 (one class dominates) to 1 (all equal). Simpson is the chance that two random points fall in different classes.
      Hill numbers give the "effective number of classes": N1 weights classes by their share, N2 counts only the common ones. Dominance is the share of the most common class.
    
  
  
    Diversity is more than counting classes
    Taxonomic indices treat every class as equally different and ignore where soils sit and how they change with depth. Our approach measures pedodiversity from continuous soil properties in three dimensions, as the organisation of energy across the soil system.
    Get in touch →
  
  Ibáñez, J.J., De-Alba, S., Bermúdez, F.F., García-Álvarez, A. (1995). Pedodiversity: concepts and measures. Catena 24, 215–232. Hill, M.O. (1973). Ecology 54, 427–432. Thermodynamic approach: Flynn, T. (2026). Preprint. doi:10.32942/X2H66M.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
What we do


Soil and landscape mapping
Depth-consistent digital soil maps, soil property surfaces and functional domains, from plot to national scale. 


Hydrology and runoff
Hydrologic soil groups, curve numbers and runoff parameters, and soil-water flux modelling across hillslopes.  


Geostatistics and uncertainty
Variograms, kriging, mixed models and uncertainty propagation, so every map comes with an honest error estimate. 


Decision support
Turning model output and its uncertainty into clear, policy-ready classes and priorities.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
How we work
RafikiArdhi takes on environmental problems where existing methods fall short. We develop a method suited to the problem, validate it against real data, and, where agreements allow, release it as an open tool so the knowledge keeps building rather than resetting with each project.
Clients get the solution, and the expertise to apply it to their own data and decisions.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
Example: making GIS depth-aware
GIS platforms treat soil as a stack of flat layers, so properties jump at every layer boundary and anything between the standard depths is lost. We built a physics-informed depth spline that runs inside Google Earth Engine, turning a spatially explicit platform into one that is also depth-aware. Each pixel carries a continuous, physically consistent profile, so properties can be read at any depth or integrated over the whole profile, and new layers such as moisture or temperature can be added to the same framework.



Soil organic carbon from the depth spline: maps at six standard depths (left) and the whole-profile total from integrating each pixel’s continuous profile (right).

title: About
text: RafikiArdhi is an independent environmental research company built on one idea: science should stay open. We publish what we produce, turn validated methods into free tools, and fund that work through the projects we take on.

title: About
text:
Open by design


We publish what we produce
Our methods go through peer review and into the scientific literature, with the details needed to reproduce them. Results that shape decisions should be open to scrutiny.


Free tools
Validated methods become free tools that anyone can use in a browser. They run on your own device, so your data never leaves it.


Paid work funds open work
Projects, advanced analyses and custom development pay for the research. As methods are proven, and agreements allow, they are released openly.


Credit where it is due
We build on other people’s work and cite it clearly: the methods, data and classification systems our tools rely on.

title: About
text:
How a method becomes open

Solve. We take on environmental problems that existing methods handle poorly.
Validate. The method is tested against independent data and published.
Release. A simplified, well-documented version becomes a free tool.
Support. The full system method, applied to your data and question, is available as a project.

title: About
section: What is free, and what is a project
text:
What is free, and what is a project


Always free
Published methods and open-access papers, the online tools, their documentation and the references behind them.


Projects
Advanced and continuous versions of the tools, analysis of your data, custom development and training. Client data stays confidential, and client-funded results are never published without an agreement.

title: About
text:
Approach
We build on existing knowledge rather than replacing it. Every map and piece of information is updated, not reset; every estimate propagates its uncertainty; and every result is explained in terms the decision maker can use.
We do not use AI to replace human expertise. Where others reach for black-box AI, we use “glass box” functions: methods that are easy to interpret, scale to large problems, and are benchmarked against AI models.
